tracks.title: The New Normal (6:00 AM)
tracks.loreNote: Following their move to the Brooks' family home in Christiansburg, Zoe initially devises a highly efficient but physically punishing commute schedule. By putting the group on the 5:45 AM Maroon Express, they beat the morning rush, but are left waiting 45 minutes in the freezing cold before the CPI campus library opens. Recognizing the severe health risk this environmental exposure poses to Jordan's medically vulnerable system, Zoe abandons her initial plan and recalculates. She determines that the 6:00 AM Blue Ridge Transit Route 1 local bus is the optimal, safe alternative—trading a longer, 45-minute ride for a vastly reduced 15-minute wait in the cold. The song is a fast, analytical, and triumphant track representing Zoe's logical system rightfully prioritizing Jordan's well-being over pure efficiency.

tracks.title: I-64 (The Gauntlet)
tracks.loreNote: This track explores the visceral, geographic nature of trauma. In an attempt to conquer his demons and see the Blue Ridge Parkway at Rockfish Gap, Jordan agrees to a road trip. However, reaching the gap requires driving on Interstate 64 East. To Jordan, I-64 is not just a highway; it is a psychological "rootkit virus," intrinsically tied to the route back to his abuser, Aubrie Sinclair, in Hampton Roads. The tension mounts during the agonizing 30-mile stretch starting in Lexington, where I-81 and I-64 merge. Despite his desire to be brave, the moment Mark actually takes Exit 221 to continue onto I-64 East in Staunton, Jordan's system catastrophically crashes. The sheer terror of being on the road heading toward his mother induces a severe meltdown, forcing Mark to immediately abort the mission and bail out at the very next ramp—Exit 91 (SR-285 towards Fishersville)—to break the virus's hold.

tracks.title: 99.8 (The Fever)
tracks.loreNote: This track highlights the lingering, practical consequences of Aubrie Sinclair's medical and emotional neglect. Jordan wakes up feeling unwell and discovers he has a low-grade temperature of 99.8°F. To a typical young adult, this is a minor inconvenience easily solved with over-the-counter medication. But because his mother deliberately weaponized his dependency by never teaching him basic self-care, health literacy, or how to handle minor illnesses, Jordan spirals into a panic. He views this slight fever as a catastrophic system failure. The "very preventable problem" is simply his lack of knowledge on how to take a Tylenol and drink fluids. The track resolves with his chosen family gently stepping in, not just to care for him, but to teach him the basic medical protocols he was maliciously denied.

tracks.title: The Leviathan Cut (A Sister's Love)
tracks.loreNote: As Jordan recovers from his fever, his chosen family decides to cheer him up with the ultimate movie marathon. Cult-following devotees Jack, Sarah, Molly, and Clare sit him down to watch the legendary, 12-hour, 21-minute "Leviathan Cut" of *The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel*. The film is an absolute 1980s cheesy fantasy adventure bliss. As the movie opens with its epic, synthesizer-and-guitar-driven anthem, "A Sister's Love (Main Theme)," Jordan is instantly captivated. The song, performed by the band Fireflight and featuring the powerful female lead vocals of Alannah Shaw, acts as a musical awakening for him. Watching the protagonist Kaelan embark on a perilous quest to save his twin sister Kaela, Jordan realizes he wants his own life's soundtrack to sound exactly like this: full of vibrant 1980s synthesizer power, driving rock energy, and unapologetic hope.

tracks.title: An 80s Education (The Brooks Mix)
tracks.loreNote: After witnessing Jordan's sheer delight at the soundtrack of *The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel*, Daniel Brooks makes it his personal mission to guide "his daughter's boy" through the greatest musical decade. Realizing that Jordan's abusive upbringing denied him the joy of popular culture, Daniel curates the ultimate, definitive mixtape: "The Brooks Mix." This track is a joyous, high-energy explosion of gated snares, analog synthesizers, and stadium rock. It represents Jordan finally shedding the cold, oppressive industrial noise of his past and joyfully embracing the neon, unapologetic optimism of the 1980s.

tracks.title: What If I'm Like Her? (Stork & Cradle)
Logically Unfounded (The Pact of Six)
tracks.loreNote: After confronting his deepest fears, Jordan still struggles with a lingering, analytical anxiety planted by his mother: the cynical idea that the unconditional love of his chosen family is "logically unfounded." Why would six people—Aubrie, Madison, Zoe, Lauren, Hannah, and Mark—dedicate themselves to his care, happiness, and protection without any ulterior motive or blood obligation? In response, the group gathers around him to formally declare "The Pact of Six." They dismantle his anxiety by explaining that love isn't a transactional equation to be balanced. Their commitment to him is not a temporary charity project; it is a permanent, foundational truth. The promise they make to him is absolute, undeniable, and crystal clear.

tracks.title: The Longest Night (NPO)
tracks.loreNote: Jordan survives the catastrophic STEMI, but the immediate aftermath introduces him to the grueling, unglamorous reality of inpatient cardiac recovery. This track captures his first night in the hospital. He is placed on strict "NPO" (nil per os / nothing by mouth) status in case he needs emergency surgery, leaving him intensely, frustratingly hungry and thirsty. To compound his misery, the nurses wake him every two hours for mandatory vitals checks, wrapping a cold blood pressure cuff around his arm just as he drifts off. Yet, amidst the sterile environment, the incessant beeping, and the gnawing hunger, there is a profound comfort: Aubrie Kelly refuses to leave his side. Sleeping in a terribly uncomfortable vinyl hospital chair, her presence transforms a night of physical misery into a quiet testament of enduring, unconditional love.

tracks.title: A CVICU Romance (Intimacy v2)
tracks.loreNote: Following his massive heart attack, Jordan is transferred to Star City General Hospital in Roanoke, where he undergoes a major CABG (Coronary Artery Bypass Graft) surgery. To ensure he is never alone in the Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit (CVICU), the single women of his pact institute a strict, rotating shift schedule. It is currently Zoe's turn when a severe blizzard strikes the Roanoke Valley, completely snowing her in. Zoe, who is also autistic, processes the world through a deeply logical, computational framework. For her, romance isn't about grand poetic gestures; it is about analyzing data, optimizing his comfort, and monitoring his telemetry. As the snow howls outside the sterile hospital window, Zoe redefines affection for Jordan. She demonstrates "Intimacy v2"—a love language built on unwavering stability, perfectly calculated care, and the beautiful logic of a system functioning exactly as it was programmed to: keeping him safe.

tracks.title: Cardiac Rehab (The Breaking Point)
tracks.loreNote: Surviving the heart attack and the CABG surgery was only the beginning; now Jordan must face the grueling, agonizing marathon of Cardiac Rehab. At just nineteen years old, he finds himself on treadmills and lifting light weights alongside patients four times his age, battling the terrifying fragility of his healing sternum and the profound exhaustion of his traumatized body. This track captures the physical and psychological "breaking point" where the pain and frustration make him want to quit entirely. However, unlike his isolated past, he is surrounded by the unbreakable wall of his chosen family. Mark acts as his spotter, Hannah brings him water, and the entire Pact of Six anchors him. When his body screams to give up, their collective strength carries him across the finish line, proving that recovery is not a solo endeavor.

tracks.title: The Accessibility Project
tracks.loreNote: Now firmly in his recovery phase and back to his coursework, Jordan and his chosen family tackle a massive class assignment: mapping CPI's accessibility features. The group realistically acknowledges that they cannot physically fix the campus—they don't have the budget to pour concrete ramps or install new elevators. However, they realize that *information* is just as powerful as infrastructure. They set out to create comprehensive maps detailing every automatic door, hidden ramp, and accessible path across the rugged terrain. A major victory in their research is mapping the "Hillside Pass-Throughs." They document the university's policy allowing disabled non-residents to get their student IDs specially encoded by the Office of Educational Accessibility. This grants 24/7 access to the 1st and 2nd-floor lobbies and the elevator of buildings built on inclines—like Jordan's old dorm, "The Old Lady on the Hill" (Eleanor Bennett Hall)—allowing students to safely bypass steep hills regardless of standard guest hours. Musically, this track is an upbeat, focused, and triumphant "heist" song, turning data collection into a grand adventure.

tracks.title: The Eleventh Child (A Gauntlet of Hearts)
tracks.loreNote: This is the grand finale. Jordan has survived the absolute worst his abuser, his own failing body, and the world could throw at him. He has crossed his own personal "Silver Gauntlet." The title, "The Eleventh Child," is a poetic metaphor to Jordan; he feels as though he was reborn and saved at the "eleventh hour," adopted into a massive, sprawling network of love as a new child of the light. (The universe holds a deeper, biological irony to this title, but to Jordan, it simply means miraculous salvation). The "Gauntlet of Hearts" refers to the unbreakable wall formed by his chosen family—the Pact of Six, the Brooks, and everyone who stood by him. Musically, this track is the ultimate 1980s stadium-rock euphoric anthem. It is loud, unapologetically joyful, and exploding with triumphant synthesizers and soaring guitars. He is 100% safe, 100% secure, and entirely free.
